narratives.narrative: The inner act here is asking (H7592), whose sense (101) is 'asked life, received it' and whose type (102) is volition - a movement of the will, not a feeling or reflex. No source is recorded (103 absent): the psalm does not trace what within the king generated the petition, so the asking stands as a bare act of will with no named internal origin. It is not organ-located (seat 104 = none) - the willing is not lodged in heart or any faculty but is a whole-self movement. The bearer (105) is the king. The operation (106) is a completed transaction: he asked life of God and received it, length of days forever - a request answered beyond measure. The target (107) is 'asking-and-receiving' itself, so the reading fixes on the coupling of petition to grant rather than on an external object. Manner is none (108): the text marks no mode, no urgency or ceremony to the asking. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are all unrecorded - the passage does not weigh the force of the request, adds no qualification, and names no inner after-state; the will simply asks and is met. Coupling (112) is 'asked-life', binding the act to its content: what is asked is life, and life defines the movement. No prohibition (113): this willing is neither restrained nor forbidden. The discovery (114, v4) confirms the shape - a specific petition (life) overfulfilled. Role (115) is characteristic: the asking is a true feature of the inner being. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the act sits within the inner life as a state of the willing self, even as God is the arena it reaches toward.
narratives.story: When the king wants life, he asks God for it plainly, and he receives far more than he asked - not just life but length of days without end. The psalm shows this as a movement of the will: a deliberate request. It does not tell us what stirred the request inside him, nor does it lodge it in any one part of him; the whole person simply asks. There is no urgency described, no measure of how hard he asked, and no note of how he felt afterward - only that he asked for life and life was given. What matters is the pairing itself: a request met, and met beyond all measure.

narratives.narrative: This deafness is not a defect but a chosen posture. Sense (101) is 'like a deaf, mute man I do not answer'; type (102) is volition - the deafness is willed, an act, not an affliction. No source is recorded (103 absent): the passage does not trace what inside the psalmist produces the silence, leaving the will's decision unexplained at its root. Seat is none (104): the deafness is not organ-located - it is not the ear that fails but the self that chooses, a whole-person stance. Bearer (105) is the psalmist. The operation (106) is that the self becomes like a deaf man who does not hear and a mute who does not open his mouth - a deliberate silence held before accusers. Target (107) is 'chosen-silence': the aim is the silence itself, a refusal to answer. Manner is none (108): no mode of the silence is marked - not its tone, not its bearing. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the text does not measure how total the silence is, adds no qualification, and names no inner consequence - the outcome is left with God (per the discovery). Coupling (112) is 'deaf-and-mute', binding not-hearing to not-speaking as one act: the refusal to hear and the refusal to answer are a single movement. No prohibition (113): the silence is not commanded or forbidden. Discovery (114, v13-14): though slandered, the interior keeps silence and leaves its case to God. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - a state of the inner self, adopted within, with the accusers as the arena it refuses to engage.
narratives.story: Surrounded by people plotting against him and spreading lies, the psalmist deliberately acts like a man who is deaf and mute - he simply will not hear their charges or answer them. This is a choice, not a disability; nothing in his body has failed. The psalm does not explain what inside him produced this restraint, and it does not measure how hard it is to keep. His refusal to listen and his refusal to speak are really one act: he shuts the whole exchange out. He holds his silence and leaves his defense to God.

narratives.narrative: Here hearing is longed for, not yet had. Sense (101) is shama, 'let me hear joy and gladness'; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent): the passage does not name the inner faculty behind the longing. Seat is none (104): the hearing is not organ-located - it is not framed as an ear's function but as the whole penitent's yearning. Bearer (105) is the penitent. Operation (106) is 'long to hear' - the act is desire straining toward a word not yet spoken. Target (107) is 'joy and gladness', a paired span: what he wants to hear is the announcement that restores gladness. Manner none (108): no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent - the text does not weigh the longing's force, qualifies it no further, and names no achieved inner result; it stays a plea. Coupling (112), also a paired span, binds the hearing to the broken bones rejoicing - the word longed for is the pardon that would make the very bones God crushed rejoice. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the plea to be told the word of pardon that turns sorrow toward hope. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the operation sits within the inner life as a longing state, reaching toward God for the word.
narratives.story: The penitent aches to hear joy and gladness again - not to make it himself, but to be told it. He does not yet have this word; the whole psalm shows him longing for it. The passage does not spell out what part of him does the longing or how intensely he feels it; it simply shows the desire straining toward a word not yet spoken. What he wants to hear is the news of pardon - and that news is tied to something almost physical: the bones God broke would themselves rejoice. His sorrow is turning, reaching toward hope.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other readings: this is a penitent's private longing to hear the word of pardon that restores joy (bearer = the penitent; locus internal), whereas the wicked readings (58:5, 59:7) are refusal and presumption, and the God-oriented readings (81:5, 85:8, 95:7) hear God's own voice directly.

narratives.narrative: This is the descent read at full weight: hearing refused. Sense (101) is shama, 'does not hear the charmers'; but type (102) is status, not action - the not-hearing is a settled condition of the wicked, a fixed state rather than a single deed. No source (103 absent): the passage does not trace where this deafness originates inside them, presenting it as simply constitutive. Seat none (104): not organ-located - the ear is 'stopped', but the deafness is of the whole self, not a failed organ. Bearer (105) is the wicked, imaged as the deaf adder. Operation (106) is 'refuse to hear / heed' - an active shutting-out. Target (107) is the voice of charmers, the cunning enchanter - every appeal and correction. Manner (108) is here present and vivid: 'stopping its ear, willfully deaf' - the mode is deliberate self-closure. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the text does not grade the deafness, adds no further qualifier, and names no inner consequence beyond the condition itself. Coupling (112), a paired span, binds the deafness to 'the incorrigibility of their venom' - the refusal to hear is one with their poison; they cannot be charmed out of it. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the willful, self-stopped deafness of the wicked, deaf to all correction and appeal. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - a state of the wicked inner being, with the charmers' voice as the arena it seals itself against.
narratives.story: The wicked are like a snake that plugs its own ears so no charmer's voice can reach it. Their refusal to listen is not a passing act but a fixed condition of who they are. The psalm does not explain where this deafness comes from inside them; it simply belongs to them. And it is deliberate - they stop their own ears on purpose, shutting out every appeal and every correction. Their unwillingness to hear is bound up with their poison: they cannot be talked out of it, because they will not let the words in.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other readings by being a settled state (type = status) of willful, self-stopped deafness in the wicked - refusal rather than reception. Unlike 59:7 (a presumption that none hears), here the refusal has a marked manner (stopping the ear) and is coupled to incorrigible venom.

narratives.narrative: The inner act here is a presumption about hearing. Sense (101) is shama, 'Who will hear us?'; type (102) is status - a settled assumption, the enemies' standing frame of mind, not a discrete deed. No source (103 absent): the passage does not name what breeds this presumption within them. Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the enemies, presuming. Operation (106): 'presume none hears' - they act on the conviction that no one, not even God, marks their words. Target (107) is explicitly none: the reading finds no object of their hearing - fittingly, since their whole point is that there is no hearer; the silence in this dimension is itself the finding, the void where a listener should be. Manner (108) is none: no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the presumption is not graded, not further qualified, and no inner after-state is recorded. Coupling (112), a paired span, binds their presumption to God's mocking laughter (v8) - the assumption that none hears is answered by the One who does, with derision. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the brazen presumption of the wicked, practical atheism, which God answers with laughter. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - a state of the enemies' inner being, oriented toward a hearer they deny.
narratives.story: The psalmist's enemies snarl their threats and think, 'Who will hear us?' - convinced no one is listening, not even God. This is not a stray thought but their settled outlook. The psalm does not say what bred this attitude in them, and it names no one they imagine hearing - that emptiness is the point: they assume there is no listener at all. But there is one. The God they think is absent hears them, and answers their arrogance with laughter.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other readings: a settled presumption (type = status) that no one hears, with an explicitly empty target and empty manner - the very void of a listener is the finding. Unlike 58:5's active self-stopping deafness, this is a denial that any hearer exists at all, answered by God's derision.

narratives.narrative: Here hearing is attentive reception. Sense (101) is shama, 'twice have I heard this'; type (102) is action - a real taking-in. No source (103 absent): the passage does not name the inner faculty of reception. Seat none (104): not organ-located; the whole self receives. Bearer (105) is the psalmist. Operation (106): 'hear / take in' - the word is received and held. Target (107), a paired span, is 'that power and steadfast love belong to God' - two truths, taken together. Manner (108), present and a paired span, is 'once God spoke, twice heard' - the mode is a numerical intensification, one speaking received as doubly certain. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no separate grading, no further qualifier, no named inner after-state - though the whole psalm's silent trust flows from this hearing. Coupling (112) is none: unlike the other readings, this hearing is not bound to a paired act - the finding stands alone, the bare reception of the two great truths. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the two truths that ground all trust - power AND steadfast love both belong to God - so the soul may safely be silent before him. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - the operation is oriented toward God, whose word is received.
narratives.story: The psalmist has heard God speak, and what he heard he holds as doubly sure: God said it once, but he has taken it in twice over. What he heard is two things held together - that all power belongs to God, and that faithful love belongs to him too. The psalm does not lodge this hearing in any one part of him; his whole self simply receives it. Unlike his other moments of hearing, this one is not tied to any further action - it stands on its own. And because both truths are true at once, his soul can rest in silence before God.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'heard' readings: this is the inward reception of God's own twofold word (locus external:god, and uniquely no coupling), whereas 66:8 causes praise to resound outward, 78:3 receives handed-down tradition, 92:11 hears the enemies' doom, and 132:6 is a report that prompts a quest.

narratives.narrative: This 'hearing' runs outward - causing to be heard. Sense (101) is shama in its causative reach, 'let the sound of his praise be heard'; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent): the passage does not name an inner origin for this making-audible. Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the peoples - a corporate inner impulse. Operation (106): 'make heard / cause to resound' - not receiving a sound but producing one, sending praise abroad. Target (107), a paired span, is 'the sound of God's praise' - what they cause to be heard. Manner none (108): no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the loudness is not graded, no further qualifier, no named inner after-state. Coupling (112), a paired span, binds the making-heard to 'blessing God' - the sounding of praise is one with blessing him. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the peoples causing his praise to be heard abroad - the public voicing of blessing. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - oriented toward God as the one praised.
narratives.story: Here the peoples are told to make God's praise heard - to send the sound of it out so everyone can catch it. This is not about taking a sound in but about giving one out, letting the praise ring abroad. The psalm does not say what stirs this inside them; it simply calls them to do it together. And making his praise heard is the same thing as blessing him - the two are one act. It is worship made public, carried to every ear.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'heard' readings: this is the outward, causative sense - making praise resound and be heard abroad (coupled with blessing God), unlike the inward receptions of 62:11 and 78:3, the hearing of judgment in 92:11, or the report that prompts a quest in 132:6.

narratives.narrative: Hearing here is summoned attention to testimony. Sense (101) is shama, 'Come and hear, all you who fear God'; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent): no inner origin named for the summoned hearing. Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is all who fear God, summoned. Operation (106): 'come and hear' - the invited act of listening to another's account. Target (107): 'what God has done for the psalmist's soul' - the object is personal testimony. Manner none (108): no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: not graded, not further qualified, no named inner after-state. Coupling (112), a paired span, binds this to the God-fearers being summoned and parallels 'come and see' (v5) - private mercy now made public witness. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the invitation to the God-fearing to listen to what God did for one soul. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - oriented toward God's deed as the thing heard.
narratives.story: The psalmist calls out to everyone who fears God: come and listen, and I will tell you what God has done for me. The hearing here is an invitation to attend to one person's testimony. The passage does not dwell on what part of the hearers does the listening; it just gathers them in. Earlier the psalm said 'come and see' what God has done; now it says 'come and hear' - the same move, turning a private mercy into public witness. One soul's rescue becomes something the whole gathering takes in.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings: this is a summons to attend to human testimony about God's deed (bearer = God-fearers summoned, target = what God did for one soul), whereas 51:8 is a private longing to hear pardon, 58:5 and 59:7 are the wicked's refusal and presumption, and 81/85/95 hear God's own voice directly.

narratives.narrative: A distinct verb - azan, 'give ear' - for summoned attention. Sense (101) is 'give ear / attend'; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent): no inner origin named. Seat none (104): not organ-located, though the idiom names the ear; the attending is of the whole people, not a lodged faculty. Bearer (105) is 'my people'. Operation (106): 'attend / give ear' - the deliberate inclining of attention to instruction. Target (107): 'the teaching that rehearses God's deeds'. Manner none (108): no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: not graded, not further qualified, no named inner after-state. Coupling (112) pairs the giving-ear with 'the received tradition (v3)' - it is bound to the handing-on of what was heard from the fathers. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): the opening call to the people to receive the instruction that will hand on God's deeds. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:person - the attention is oriented toward a human teacher, not directly toward God, which distinguishes it from the shama readings that hear God's own voice.
narratives.story: The teacher opens by calling the people to give ear - to lean in and pay attention to his instruction. This is a deliberate turning of attention toward what is being taught: the story of what God has done. The psalm does not say what stirs the people to listen; it simply summons them. And their listening is tied to a chain of handing-on - what the fathers told is now passed to the next generation. Notably, the ear here is turned toward a human voice teaching, not toward God speaking directly.

narratives.narrative: Hearing here is the reception of tradition. Sense (101) is shama, 'things that we have heard and known'; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent): no inner origin named for the reception. Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is 'we', the psalmist's generation. Operation (106): 'receive by hearing' - taking in what was told. Target (107): 'the things heard and known' - the content of the tradition. Manner none (108): no mode marked. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: not graded, not further qualified, no named inner after-state. Coupling (112) pairs hearing with 'knowing and the fathers' telling' - it is bound to knowing and to the prior act of the fathers who told. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): tradition taken in by hearing, faith received before it is understood. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the reception lodges within the inner being as its own held knowledge, distinct from 78:1 (the same passage) whose ear was turned outward to a human teacher; here the hearing has become inward possession ('heard and known').
narratives.story: The psalmist speaks of things 'we have heard and known' - the stories the fathers told, taken in by listening. This hearing is a receiving: the past generation spoke, and this one took their words in. The passage does not spell out how the receiving works inside them; it simply happened. Hearing here is bound up with knowing and with the fathers' telling - what was passed down has become something the hearers now hold as their own. Faith is received by ear before it is fully understood.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'heard' readings: this is the inward taking-in of handed-down tradition become known (locus internal:ib-state), versus the outward causing of praise to resound (66:8), the reception of God's direct word (62:11), the hearing of enemies' doom (92:11), or the report that prompts a quest (132:6).

narratives.narrative: Hearing at a threshold - the reception of divine speech. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the psalmist / Israel. Operation (106): 'hear / receive'. Target (107): 'a voice/language not known' - the object is speech previously unfamiliar, God's own voice breaking in. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the reception is not graded, not further qualified, and no inner after-state is named. Coupling (112) pairs this hearing with 'the oracle that follows' - it is the hinge that opens onto God's speech in the rest of the psalm. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v5): the prophetic receiving of God's voice, the hinge where the psalm turns to divine speech. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - oriented toward God as speaker.
narratives.story: At a turning point the psalmist says he hears a voice he had not known before - God's own voice beginning to speak. This hearing is a receiving: a word arrives that was not his own. The passage does not explain how it lands inside him; it simply marks the moment the unfamiliar voice is caught. And it is a hinge: right after this, the psalm becomes God speaking directly. The listener stands at the doorway of an oracle.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings: this is the reception of God's own unfamiliar voice at the psalm's hinge (target = a voice not known), unlike the outward summons to others (81:8), the wicked's refusal (58:5), or the penitent's plea for pardon (51:8).

narratives.narrative: Here God summons to be heard. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action - the demanded attention. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is 'my people'. Operation (106): 'hear / attend'. Target (107): 'God's admonition' - what is to be heard is correction. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: not graded, not further qualified, no named inner after-state. Coupling (112) pairs this hearing with 'the plea to listen' - the companion clause of v8 - so the summoned hearing is bound to the very next call to heed. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v8): the summoned attention, God pleading to be heard. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - God is both the one who calls and the one to be heard. This reading is deliberately kept distinct from #7 at the same verse: the outward summons to hear is not the same movement as the inner disposition to heed.
narratives.story: God calls to his people: hear me while I warn you. This is a demand for attention - the people are to take in God's correction. The passage does not describe the inner workings of their listening; it simply issues the call. And the call comes doubled: 'hear me' is immediately joined by a plea that they would truly heed. It is God asking, almost pleading, to be listened to.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings, and specifically from #7 at the same verse (81:8): this is the outward summons to hear God's admonition (type = action, bearer = God's people), whereas #7 reads the answering disposition to heed. It also differs from #5's reception of the unknown voice by being a demand rather than a receiving.

narratives.narrative: The same verse yields a second, distinct reading - not the summons but the disposition it hopes for. Sense (101) is shama as 'listen'; type (102) here is disposition, not action - a settled inclination to heed, and this shift from a called act to an inner bent is precisely what separates it from #6. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is Israel. Operation (106): 'listen / heed'. Target (107): God himself - not merely his words but him. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the disposition is not graded, not further qualified, and no achieved after-state is named - fitting, since it is only wished for. Coupling (112) pairs it with 'the summons to hear' (#6) - the disposition is the hoped-for answer to the call. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114): 'O Israel, if you would but listen to me!' - the wistful conditional on which the whole tragedy hangs. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god. Preserving #6 and #7 as distinct is itself a finding: the outward summons and the inner readiness to heed are not the same movement.
narratives.story: In the same breath God adds a wish: 'If only you would listen to me!' This is different from the command to hear - it points to an inner willingness, a readiness of heart to heed. What is longed for is not just attention to God's words but a turning toward God himself. It is spoken as a wistful 'if only', and the whole sorrow of the psalm hangs on it. The call to hear and the hoped-for willingness to obey are kept apart on purpose - they are not the same thing.
narratives.variation_note: Distinguished from #6 at the same verse (81:8) by type: this is a heeding disposition toward God himself, not the outward summons. It also differs from the receiving readings (81:5, 85:8) by being the inner bent of the will rather than the act of reception.

narratives.narrative: Hearing as the posture of attentive faith. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the psalmist. Operation (106): 'hear / listen' - a chosen readiness. Target (107): 'to what God will speak' - the object is a word not yet uttered; the hearer waits. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the waiting is not graded, not further qualified, and no after-state is named - though the coupling anticipates one. Coupling (112) pairs this hearing with 'the peace God speaks' - it leans toward the shalom God will pronounce to his people. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v8): the posture of attentive faith, waiting on God's word of peace. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - oriented toward God as speaker.
narratives.story: The psalmist quiets himself to hear what God will say. This is the stance of waiting faith: he does not yet have the word, so he listens for it. The passage does not describe the inner workings of this listening; it simply shows him poised and attentive. And what he expects to hear is peace - God speaking calm and well-being over his people. His whole posture is one of trusting readiness for a word about to come.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings: this is expectant waiting on God's not-yet-spoken word of peace (bearer = the psalmist, target = what God will speak), unlike the already-received word (62:11), the summons to others (66:16, 81:8), or Zion's glad hearing of accomplished judgments (97:8).

narratives.narrative: Hearing here confirms vindication - and it is read with the same weight as any gladder hearing (no valence bias). Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located, though 'my ears' is named - the perceiving is of the whole self, not a lodged faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist. Operation (106): 'hear'. Target (107): 'the doom of his evil assailants' - what is heard is the downfall of enemies, a hard and satisfying report. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the hearing is not graded, not further qualified, and no separate after-state row is written. The coupling (112) and locus (116) fields carry pairing values that read together: the hearing is bound to seeing their downfall and sits as an internal ib-state - ear and eye together register the enemies' end within the inner life. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v11): the hearing of the wicked's judgment, vindication confirmed to the senses. Role (115) is characteristic.
narratives.story: The psalmist says his own ears have heard the downfall of the men who set themselves against him. This is a hearing of judgment - the report that his enemies have met their doom, and it is received with satisfaction, not shrunk from. The passage does not measure how deeply it registers; it simply notes that he heard it. And what his ears hear, his eyes also see: hearing and sight together take in the enemies' ruin. The confirmation settles inside him as vindication made real to his senses.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'heard' readings: this hears the enemies' doom - a hard vindication received into the inner life and paired with seeing their downfall - unlike the reception of God's gracious word (62:11), the outward voicing of praise (66:8), the handed-down tradition (78:3), or the report that prompts worship (132:6).

narratives.narrative: Hearing as the urgent 'today'. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the people. Operation (106): 'hear / heed' - attention that must become obedience. Target (107): God's voice 'today' - the object is God's present address, time-stamped now. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no separate grading or qualifier; the after-state is carried by the paired clause. The coupling (112) and locus (116) fields read together: the hearing is oriented toward God and paired with 'not hardening the heart' - to hear is set directly against the hardening that Meribah shows. No prohibition (113) is separately recorded, though the paired warning against hardening functions as the negative edge of the summons. Discovery (114, v7): the summons to heed God now, the hinge from praise to warning. Role (115) is characteristic.
narratives.story: 'Today, if you hear his voice' - the psalm turns from praise to urgent appeal. Hearing here is meant to become obedience, and the moment is now, not later. The passage does not measure how the hearing works inside; it simply presses the 'today'. What is to be heard is God's own voice, addressed to the people in the present. And it comes with its shadow warning: do not harden your hearts, as an earlier generation did in the wilderness. To hear is set squarely against that hardening.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings: this is the urgent present summons to heed God's voice 'today', set against heart-hardening - distinct from Zion's glad hearing of settled judgments (97:8), the expectant waiting for peace (85:8), and the wicked's flat refusal (58:5).

narratives.narrative: Hearing that issues in gladness. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is Zion - a corporate inner subject. Operation (106): 'hear'. Target (107): 'of God's judgments' - what is heard is news of God's just reign. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the hearing is not graded, not further qualified, and no separate effect row is written - yet the paired locus field supplies the outcome. The coupling (112) and locus (116) fields read together: an internal ib-state paired with 'being glad' - hearing and gladness are one inward movement. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v8): the holy city receiving news of God's just reign, hearing that gladdens. Role (115) is characteristic.
narratives.story: Zion hears the news of how God has judged the world, and the hearing turns at once to joy. Here listening and gladness are a single inward motion - to take in this news is to rejoice. The passage does not spell out the mechanics or measure the joy; it simply reports that the city heard and was glad. What gladdens is God's just reign, his judgments made known. The report lands inside the people as delight.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'hear' readings: this hearing lands in immediate gladness at God's accomplished judgments (bearer = Zion, paired with being glad), unlike the urgent still-open summons (95:7), the expectant waiting (85:8), or the hard hearing of enemies' doom (92:11).

narratives.narrative: The descent, read at full weight: listening that fails. Sense (101) is shama, marked 'failed' - the very word for heeding is used of its absence. Type (102) is disposition: the not-listening is a settled inclination, a bent of the will, not a one-off lapse. No source (103 absent): the passage does not trace what within the people produces the refusal - it stands as a fact of their disposition. Seat none (104): not organ-located; the whole self will not heed. Bearer (105) is 'my people'. Operation (106): 'fail to listen' - an active non-heeding. Target (107): 'to God's voice' - what is refused is God's own address. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent here - though the psalm's next line (God giving them over to their stubborn hearts) is the consequence, this reading records no effect row, leaving the failure itself as the finding. Coupling (112) pairs the not-listening with 'the refusal to submit' - not-heeding is bound to not-yielding; the two are one movement of the will. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v11): the tragic refusal, the summons of v8 met with deafness. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god - oriented against God as the one refused.
narratives.story: God's people simply would not listen to him. This is not a single slip but a set disposition - a turning of the will away from his voice. The psalm does not explain what produced the refusal inside them; it presents it as who they had become. And it is bound to something deeper: they would not listen because they would not yield. The earlier call to hear is here met with flat deafness - the will refusing both to heed and to submit.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from #2 (v13, same passage): this is the accomplished refusal - the people's settled failure to heed God's voice, coupled with their refusal to submit (a descent), whereas #2 is God's own unfulfilled longing that they would listen.

narratives.narrative: The counterpart to the refusal - the same heeding, now as unfulfilled longing. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is disposition - the desired settled inclination to heed. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is 'my people' - the same people who failed in v11, now the object of a wish. Operation (106): 'listen / heed' - what God longs for. Target (107): God himself. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: the longing is not graded, not further qualified, and no achieved after-state is named - precisely because it goes unmet. Coupling (112) pairs the hoped-for listening with 'walking in his ways' - to heed would be to walk with God. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v13): the divine longing, grief and love in one breath. Role (115) is characteristic. Locus (116) is external:god. Held beside #1, the pairing is the finding: the refusal (v11) and the yearning (v13) frame the same heeding as failure and as ache.
narratives.story: 'Oh, that my people would listen to me!' - God's grief and love spoken together. Against their refusal stands his longing: he wishes they would truly heed him. This is a desire for a settled willingness of heart, not just passing attention. And to listen would mean to live it out - to walk in his ways. The passage sets this yearning right beside their earlier refusal, so the same act of heeding appears twice: once as their failure, and once as God's aching wish.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from #1 (v11, same passage): the same heeding read as God's unfulfilled longing (coupled with walking in his ways), not the people's accomplished refusal - the two together frame heeding as both failure and ache.

narratives.narrative: Hearing that sets a search in motion. Sense (101) is shama; type (102) is action. No source (103 absent). Seat none (104): not organ-located. Bearer (105) is the people. Operation (106): 'hear of the ark' - a report received. Target (107): 'and seek it' - the object of the hearing is not merely the news but the quest it triggers; hearing passes straight into seeking. Manner none (108). Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent as separate rows - yet the movement to seek and worship is the very substance of this hearing. The coupling (112) and locus (116) fields read together: oriented toward God and paired with 'going to worship' - the report heard becomes a pilgrimage. No prohibition (113). Discovery (114, v6): the people's report of the ark, the hearing that moves them to seek and worship. Role (115) is characteristic.
narratives.story: The people heard word of the ark - a report that reached them at Ephrathah. But this hearing did not stop at news; it set them searching, and then moving out to worship. To hear of God's presence was to go looking for it and to bow before it. The passage does not dwell on how the report worked inside them; it simply shows hearing turning into a quest. What they heard sent them on pilgrimage toward the place where God would dwell.
narratives.variation_note: Differs from the item's other 'heard' readings: this hearing is a report that ignites a search and worship (operation = hear of the ark, target = seek it, paired with going to worship), unlike the inward reception of God's word (62:11), the causing of praise to resound (66:8), the handed-down tradition (78:3), or the hearing of enemies' doom (92:11).
